title.narrative: Lonac pro - Collective Impact for Youth, MOZAIK
Lonac pro - Collective Impact for Youth, MOZAIK

description.narrative:
The overall objective during the intervention of 3 years id to strengthen sustainable, country-wide, multi-stakeholder and value -driven ecosystem that provides ongoing and tailor-made opportunities for any young women and men, regardless of their identities or location in succeeding in the social and/or economic sector in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The impact and goal of the intervention will be achieved through three outcomes whereby each outcome has further outputs and respective activities aimed at meeting the overall objective. Three listed outcomes are as follows: 1) strong and lasting partnerships with the local authorities established that directly influence use of available public resources to provide support to young female and male entrepreneurs. 2) Strong ecosystem for start up entrepreneurship and philanthropy is established within the community Lonac.pro with partnerships that create various opportunities for professional success of young women and men. 3) To design and deliver meaningful and tailor-made opportunities for young female and male entrepreneurs to start their own sustainable micro-businesses.
More specifically, expected results such as creation of 300 jobs, implementation of 300 community projects aimed at improving local communities, successful disbursement of grants to facilitate establishment and growth of micro-business, building sustainable relationships with local authorities, building capacities of young women and men to further develop in social and economic realm of the society contribute to an objective of reaching sustainable systematic solution.

Over the three-year intervention period (March 2022April 2025), the project has generated significant social, economic, and institutional impacts that extend beyond its original scope. The initiative successfully built a nationwide, multi-stakeholder youth ecosystem that links municipalities, an online platform (Rolify formally known as Lonac.Pro), YouthBank participatory grantmaking, Startup Studios, mentors, and private-sector partners. These components worked together to create opportunities for youth empowerment, entrepreneurship, and community-led development.
It includes initiatives such as Startup development through workshops like Startup Navigator., Social innovation via events, interviews, and opportunities., YouthBank activities, which fund youth-led community projects. It also provides as a networking hub for young professionals, NGOs, and entrepreneurs.
The results are notable both quantitatively and qualitatively. By June 2025, Rolify had 111,983 registered users, with 49,867 joining during the Sida-supported period. The platform facilitated 1,683 published opportunities, representing a total estimated value of approximately 4.1 million BAM. YouthBank boards implemented 305 youth-led community projects with municipal co-financing, mobilizing over 1.77 million BAM41 percent higher than originally targeted. Importantly, 24 municipalities have now created a dedicated YouthBank budget line, an important step toward long-term institutional sustainability.
The project also created a strong pipeline of youth entrepreneurship. A total of 231 microbusinesses were supported, including 192 newly launched ventures and 39 that scaled through growth grants and technical assistance. These microbusinesses achieved a high survival rate of around 87 percent and contributed to the creation of 244 jobs, 118 of which are held by women. This takes into account duration of the project however the earlier interventions served as a strong foundation to achieve these results.
In addition to these expected outcomes, the program produced several unexpected impacts. Municipal contributions significantly overshot initial projections, indicating stronger-than-anticipated buy-in from local governments. Rolify underwent a strategic pivot from a general networking platform to a skills-first system with modular learning and verification features, which accelerated employer alignment and improved user retention. The program also had to adapt to local political cycles and youth migration, which created operational challenges but ultimately led to the development of stronger onboarding systems and institutional memory tools. * In this case onbaording is a tailored approach to guide users through creating a profile, joining groups, applying for opportunities or accessing learning resources.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
